catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbacy-nulliu: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbacy Nullius of Wettingen-Mehrerau — the Cistercian abbey on Lake Constance — recounts its history and privileges. Michael Ott details this exempt abbey's story. A precise reference on a notable monastery. The Cistercians' white monks still keep its choir offices today.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-hirs: A 1913 piece on Hirschau — Hirsau in the Black Forest, mother of reform. Its customs spread through Germany. George Cyprian Alston details its work. The Cluny of the German lands. William, its great abbot, ruled like a prince of the Church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrew-of-lon: This 1913 reference article on Andrew of Lonjumeau — the Dominican envoy to the Mongols. Thomas Schwertner tells his journeys. He carried the pope's letters east. The Great Khan heard his message. A friar at the world's edge. His report amazed the Paris court.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-godea: This 1913 reference article on Antoine Godeau — the bishop-poet of the Academy. F.M. Rudge praises his verse and zeal. He left the salon for the see. Vence's bishop wrote psalms. A prelate of the grand siècle. His psalms are still sung in Vence.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-armand-benjam: A 1913 entry on Armand-Benjamin Caillau — a French churchman of note. Joseph Sollier records his works. The entry preserves his modest fame. His pen served the Paris church. A priest among the writers. His devotions fed the Paris faithful. His order honors its devout son.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-armand-hippol: This 1913 reference piece on Fizeau — the measurer of light's speed. William Fox honors his brilliant experiments. His toothed wheel caught the sunbeam. The Academy crowned his labors. A Catholic among the physicists. His name marks the Paris streets. His pendulum proved the earth's spin.
